level_3.text:
You descend deeper into the facility. Level 3 is colder. The lights here are red and most are broken.

At the end of a long hallway, you find a massive containment chamber. The glass is shattered. Whatever was held here is long gone.

But on the floor, scratched into the metal, are the words: 'WE SHOULD NEVER HAVE DUG THIS DEEP.'

A sound behind you. Breathing. Not your own.

choices.text: Stand your ground and face the creature

shoot_creature.text:
You spin around, gun already raised. In the red half-light you see it — a towering, gaunt figure with too-long arms and skin like cracked stone.

It lunges. You fire.

The shot echoes through the corridor like thunder. The creature staggers, shrieks — a sound like tearing metal — and collapses. It twitches once, then goes still.

Your hands are shaking. But it's dead. You step over the body and find a maintenance ladder behind the containment chamber.

You climb. You climb until you see sky.

You emerge into cold, sweet air. Whatever that thing was, it won't follow anyone else.

face_creature.text:
You steel yourself and turn around. In the red half-light, you see it — a towering, gaunt figure with too-long arms and skin like cracked stone.

It tilts its head. Studying you. You don't flinch.

Minutes pass. Or maybe hours. Then it steps aside, revealing a passage behind it — one not on any map. The creature watches as you walk through.

The passage leads to a ladder. The ladder leads to the sky.

You emerge into dawn, forever changed by what you faced below.

sprint_exit.text:
Your reflexes kick in before your fear does. You pivot and sprint — ducking under pipes, vaulting over debris, taking corners at full speed.

The breathing follows you, but you're faster. You burst through door after door, up staircases, through a final fire exit —

Cold air. Stars. Grass under your feet.

You don't stop until your legs give out on a hillside, the facility far behind you.

panic_run.text:
You run. You run faster than you've ever run, through corridors that blur together, up stairs, through doors — until you burst outside into cold, sweet air.

You don't stop running until the facility is just a dot on the horizon. You're alive, but shaken to your core.
